item.title: Impact of coupling a constitutive model with the ductile fracture criterion on the computational predictability of wrought Inconel 718
item.description: 库内相似论文：A study of inconel 718 dependency on stress triaxiality and lode angle in plastic deformation and ductile fracture（相似度 0.742） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：Lode dependent plasticity coupled with nonlinear damage accumulation for ductile fracture of aluminium alloy [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matdes.2017.09.064] 与《Fracture of laser powder bed fusion additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V under multiaxial loading: Calibration and comparison of fracture models》共享 8 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.138 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1977188519, https://openalex.org/W2016463190, https://openalex.org/W2018437493, https://openalex.org/W2032768430, https://openalex.org/W2047940007 https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Impact+of+coupling+a+constitutive+model+with+the+ductile+fracture+criterion+on+the+computa&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1177%2F10567895261490276%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Prediction of ductile fracture is essential for designing of components and structures. Local uncoupled and local as well as non-local partially coupled models are compared for tensile tests of specimens made from nickel-based superalloy Inconel 718 with varying geometries: a smooth cylindrical specimen, notched cylindrical specimens with R2.5 and R8 and a flat plate specimen. The ductile fracture criterion was calibrated using a hybrid experimental–numerical approach, with the non-local part based on strain in the loading direction measured optically on a notched specimen. Models are compared with respect to force responses, moment of crack initiation and appearance of final failure. All numerical simulations, including a mesh sensitivity study, were performed in LS-DYNA software using the Newmark implicit time integration scheme. Globally, the non-local approach does not seem to be ready for solving bulky spatial problems. Published: 2026-10-12T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: International Journal of Damage Mechanics 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考 重点作者新作: František Šebek, Petr Kubík

item.title: Triaxiality-dependent asymmetric plasticity model covering a wide range of stress states for magnesium alloy sheets: Modeling shear and near-plane strain anisotropy
item.description: 库内相似论文：An improved yield criterion characterizing the anisotropic and tension-compression asymmetric behavior of magnesium alloy（相似度 0.797） 引用重点论文：On stress-state dependent plasticity modeling: Significance of the hydrostatic stress, the third invariant of stress deviator and the non-associated flow rule [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2010.05.004] 与《A lode-dependent https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Triaxiality-dependent+asymmetric+plasticity+model+covering+a+wide+range+of+stress+states+f&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jma.2026.102326%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The pronounced tension-compression asymmetry and anisotropy are common problems that severely restrict the forming accuracy of magnesium alloy components. An effective solution strategy involves adopting high-precision yield criteria capable of reconstructing material properties to optimize process parameters. In this work, a novel anisotropic-asymmetric yield criterion based on a coupling strategy of polynomial functions and stress triaxiality is proposed. The model delivers high flexibility and accuracy in capturing the anisotropic and strongly asymmetric response of magnesium alloy sheets, as validated on eight widely different virtual material cases. A systematic calibration procedure for determining the material parameters in both the yield stress function and the plastic potential function of the new model is also provided. Finally, the proposed model was applied to the AZ31 and AZ31B magnesium alloy sheets with markedly different yield loci. Compared with the CPB06ex2, Hu2017, and Zhou2023 asymmetric yield criteria, the new model achieves accurate predictions for 15 stress-related sampling points and 12 strain-related sampling points across six stress states, demonstrating comprehensively superior prediction accuracy. More importantly, the new model accurately captures the anisotropic response characteristics of the AZ31 and AZ31B magnesium alloy sheets under shear and near-plane strain stress states, strongly confirming its accuracy and applicability. item.title: Dynamic Compressive Behavior and Deformation-Failure Characteristics of a Medium-Carbon Cr-Ni-Mo High-Strength Steel

To investigate the dynamic compressive behavior and deformation characteristics of medium-carbon Cr-Ni-Mo high-strength steel under different strain rates and temperatures, quasi-static tensile and compression tests, together with Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) dynamic compression tests, were conducted. The Johnson–Cook flow stress and damage model parameters were calibrated based on the experimental results under the investigated loading conditions. Combined with macroscopic morphologies of recovered specimens, SEM fracture observations, and finite element simulations, the deformation and damage behavior of the material was investigated. The results show that the material exhibits pronounced strain-rate strengthening and thermal softening characteristics. At 298 K, increasing the strain rate from 1000 to 5000 s−1 increases the mean maximum compressive stress from 2263.1 to 2500.9 MPa, while expanding the plastic deformation range. At 1000 s−1, increasing the temperature from 298 to 698 K decreases the mean maximum compressive stress from 2263.1 to 1722.2 MPa. The calibrated Johnson–Cook model reasonably describes the stress response and deformation characteristics at different strain rates at 298 K, with relative errors of simulated maximum compressive stresses below 4% for the representative experimental curves used in the numerical comparison. The macroscopic and microscopic observations reveal that increasing strain rate promotes the localized shear deformation, inclined cracking, and partial fragmentation after plastic compression, with enhanced shear deformation features reflected by elongated dimples, fracture steps, and tear ridges. Increasing temperature reduces fragmentation under high strain-rate loading and promotes the formation of coarse dimples and plastic flow features. Numerical analysis further indicates that increasing strain rate promotes the localization of equivalent plastic strain, leading to inclined shear bands and crack formation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Genetic+algorithm%E2%80%93based+calibration+of+the+Johnson%E2%80%93Cook+fracture+model+for+high+strain+rat&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijimpeng.2026.105922%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%2C+%22impact_validation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Recent studies have increasingly employed optimization algorithms, including genetic algorithms, to identify Johnson–Cook material model parameters while reducing the experimental burden required for conventional parameter identification. However, most of these studies are based on material behavior obtained from low-strain rate tests, such as quasi-static tensile tests and notched specimen tests and therefore may not fully capture the coupled effects of strain rate dependence and damage evolution occurring during high-velocity impact. To address this limitation, the present study performed genetic algorithm-based optimization using Taylor impact test results and calibrated the Johnson–Cook fracture model parameters of aluminum 6061-T6 while keeping D 5 fixed at the literature-reported value. The derived parameters were D 1 = −0.583, D 2 = 1.451, D 3 = −0.378, and D 4 = 0.002. The calibrated parameter set was further assessed through high-velocity impact simulations of 6 mm and 8 mm thick aluminum 6061-T6 plates under a different impact configuration using the same literature-derived material data. The predicted penetration speeds and diameters showed good agreement with experimental measurements, with maximum deviations of 7.18% in penetration speed and 2.94% in penetration diameter for 6 mm and 8 mm thick plates under high-velocity impact conditions. Beyond final-state agreement, the energy erosion responses were compared using target-plate internal energy, eroded volume fraction, and eroded internal energy. These quantities were used as supplementary numerical indicators to assess element-deletion-related energy loss within the adopted finite element framework. The repeatability of the identified parameter set with respect to stochastic variability in the GA remains to be further assessed through repeated optimizations using different random seeds. Abstract Accurate characterization of flow-stress behavior is essential for modeling the dynamic deformation and machining response of titanium alloys. In this study, the mechanical behavior of near-alpha TA19 titanium alloy was investigated by quasi-static compression tests at strain rates of 0.001-0.01 s-1 and split Hopkinson pressure bar tests at 25-650 °C and 1500-4500 s-1. Strain-rate sensitivity, thermal softening, and adiabatic temperature rise were analyzed, and measured flow stresses were corrected to obtain isothermal stress-strain curves. Power-Law (PL) and Johnson-Cook (JC) constitutive models were calibrated using the same experimental dataset and quantitatively evaluated. TA19 exhibited positive strain-rate sensitivity and pronounced thermal softening. As the strain rate increased from 1500 to 4500 s-1, the average flow stress increased by 112.447-228.009 MPa, depending on temperature, whereas increasing the temperature from 25 to 650 °C reduced it by 205.226-294.361 MPa. Adiabatic heating increased with strain rate at room temperature but was generally suppressed at elevated initial temperatures. Under 16 dynamic conditions, the PL and JC models produced average absolute relative error ranges of 1.20%-7.24% and 1.54%-12.38%, respectively, with overall values of 3.85% and 6.36%. The PL model therefore provided higher overall prediction accuracy, whereas the JC model offered better numerical compatibility for engineering simulation. The calibrated JC model was implemented in AdvantEdge to investigate the effects of feed rate, cutting speed, and rake angle. Increasing feed rate reduced shear strain, plastic strain rate, and normalized cutting loads. Increasing cutting speed markedly increased plastic strain rate and redistributed the load between the cutting- and thrust-force components. A larger rake angle facilitated chip flow and reduced cutting temperature and normalized thrust force. These results clarify the coupled effects of strain hardening, strain-rate strengthening, thermal softening, and tool-chip interaction and provide a basis for constitutive-model selection and cutting-parameter optimization of TA19 titanium alloy. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Microstructural+degradation+and+impact+toughness+of+simulated+heat-affected+sub-zones+in+R&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.msea.2026.151213%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22ductile_fracture%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Medium-Mn steels exhibit excellent combinations of strength and ductility due to the presence of metastable retained austenite (RA). However, the influence of welding thermal cycles on the fracture behavior of individual heat-affected zone (HAZ) subzones remains insufficiently understood. In the present study, Gleeble-based simulations of intercritical (ICHAZ), fine-grained (FGHAZ), and coarse-grained (CGHAZ) heat-affected zones were performed on an intercritically annealed 5Mn steel with a ferritic–austenitic duplex microstructure containing approximately 30 % RA. Increasing a peak temperature progressively degraded the duplex microstructure through RA destabilization and fresh-martensite formation. The ICHAZ retained a partially duplex character, whereas the FGHAZ became predominantly martensitic, and the CGHAZ transformed into a fully martensitic microstructure. No softened HAZ region was identified; under the applied cooling conditions, diffusional transformations were suppressed and martensitic transformation predominated. Importantly, the hardness distribution was non-monotonic: the maximum hardness occurred in the fully austenitized region before pronounced prior-austenite grain coarsening, whereas further overheating toward the CGHAZ center reduced hardness despite complete martensitic transformation. Instrumented Charpy impact testing combined with fractographic analysis showed progressive deterioration of impact toughness and transition from fully ductile fracture in the base material to mixed ductile–brittle fracture in the simulated HAZ subzones. The results further showed that welding-induced microstructural degradation affected not only the total absorbed energy but also the relative contributions of crack initiation and propagation. The beneficial contribution of RA to impact toughness was strongly dependent on its stability: sufficiently stable RA was associated with enhanced plastic accommodation and crack-propagation resistance, whereas thermal destabilization and fresh-martensite formation were associated with reduced dynamic fracture resistance. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Deep+Learning-Based+Inverse+Identification+of+the+Johnson%E2%80%93Cook+Yield+and+Fracture+Paramete&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fcryst16100649%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22calibration%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Finite element analysis (FEA) is a key tool for predicting the mechanical behavior of additively manufactured parts. However, its predictive accuracy relies on the underlying constitutive model and, in particular, on precise model parameters. The main purpose of this study is to develop and validate a condition-grouped multimodal deep learning framework for efficiently identifying the ten parameters of the Johnson–Cook (JC) yield and fracture models for Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) alloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) using batch finite element simulation data. Using nearly 20,000 simulation datasets and response images covering different temperatures, strain rates, and stress triaxialities, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), long short-term memory (LSTM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models are trained to capture both sequential and physical features of the stress–strain responses. Grouping the data by test condition decouples the coupled model parameters and improves prediction accuracy. The identified yield parameters give R2 values consistently above 0.94, and the stress–strain curves reconstructed from the identified parameters agree well with experimental data (R = 0.976). The failure parameters reproduce the main fracture characteristics in simulation, but the post-peak behavior remains subject to uncertainty. The proposed method therefore allows the corresponding JC parameters to be determined directly from stress–strain curves, providing a fast route for calibrating constitutive models of TC4 components. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Micromechanics-informed+coupled+viscoplastic%E2%80%93damage+model+for+voided+composites+with+non-a&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijplas.2026.104837%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22stress_state%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The plastic flow direction in voided particulate composites does not coincide with the outward normal to the yield surface, a deviation quantified here at a mean angular error of 23.3° across 1,001 multiaxial micromechanical stress states — establishing that non-associated flow is a physically necessary and micromechanically verifiable feature of this material class. A micromechanics-informed, fully coupled viscoplastic–damage constitutive model is developed in which the yield surface — closed in the hydrostatic direction, Lode-angle dependent, and verified convex over the full calibration domain, along with the plastic potential and hardening law, are each derived from multiaxial micromechanical homogenization data rather than postulated or fitted to macroscopic experiments; the coupled evolution laws are shown to satisfy the dissipation inequality over the admissible stress domain, establishing thermodynamic admissibility. A single invariant-based criterion governs both compression-dominated viscoplastic flow and tension-dominated brittle damage through a crack-band regularized Rankine criterion, allowing regime transitions without separate criteria. The framework is implemented as an open-source user-material subroutine for Abaqus/Explicit and validated against quasi-static and dynamic experiments across three orders of magnitude in strain rate. Peak-force predictions agree with the quasi-static and dynamic experiments to within 3.0% and 1.1%, respectively, and the model reproduces without recalibration the experimentally observed 27% increase in peak force from quasi-static to dynamic loading. Although calibrated for a specific grade, the constitutive structure is grade-agnostic and directly extensible to the broader class of voided particulate composites and porous resin systems. The user-material is provided as supplementary material. Published: 2026-09-27T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: International Journal of Plasticity 研究类型: 其他相关研究

https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+SELECTION+OF+THE+STRAIN+RATE+CHANGE+MODE+DURING+HIGH-TEMPERATURE+FLAT-DIE+UPSETTING+OF+CYL&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.37128%2F2306-8744-2026-3-10%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22stress_state%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The paper considers the problem of selecting a rational mode of strain rate change during high-temperature isothermal flat-die upsetting of cylindrical billets. The object of the study is the hot upsetting process; the subject is the law of strain rate change at the critical point of the billet and the corresponding law of motion of the deforming tool. The relevance of the work stems from the fact that upsetting is one of the most energy-intensive forging operations, while the tool speed is in practice assigned as a constant value based on equipment capabilities rather than on conditions for the fullest use of the plastic capacity of the material. Known results on the optimization of the rate mode of multistage hot deformation have been obtained for processes with a homogeneous stress-strain state, for which the stress triaxiality ratio remains unchanged. During flat-die upsetting this ratio at the critical point on the equator of the lateral surface changes during the process due to barrelling, which formally makes the direct transfer of known results impossible. To overcome this obstacle, a hypothesis is formulated on the weak dependence of the limiting strain on the stress triaxiality ratio during high-temperature deformation for a certain class of materials. It is shown that a weakened form of the hypothesis is sufficient for a correct transfer of the results, requiring independence from the triaxiality ratio only for the strain rate sensitivity exponent. It is established that the resource dependence parameter enters exclusively into the scale factor of the solution and does not affect the shape of the optimal trajectory, while the relative error of the limiting strain is smaller than the relative error of this parameter. The problem of matching the optimal law of strain rate change with the tool kinematics is solved. A closed-form analytical expression for the tool speed is obtained, which does not require numerical inversion of the dependence of strain intensity on the upsetting ratio. For exponential and polynomial trajectories the law of tool motion is presented in explicit form. An estimate of the strain rate deviation within a stage is proposed, which gives the number of stages a specific technological meaning. A numerical calculation for 14Kh17N2 steel at 1150 °C established that the plastic resource of the material is not exhausted during flat-die upsetting, i.e. the process is limited geometrically rather than by deformation. For such materials the problem of minimizing the process time is meaningful. A relation is obtained linking the reduction of deformation time with the increase of the limiting strain; it is shown that an increase of the limiting strain by 5.9 % corresponds to a reduction of the upsetting time by 47 %. The conditions for applicability of the obtained results to processes of local deformation by roller burnishing are determined. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Influence+of+cryogenic+pretreatment+and+minimum+quantity+lubrication+on+grinding+character&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.matdes.2026.117178%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%2C+%22temperature%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4 V (AM Ti-64) offers excellent strength; however, its high hardness and limited ductility make grinding difficult. This study investigates the effect of cryogenic treatment at − 1 9 1 ° C on the grindability of AM Ti-64 and compares stress-relieved and stress-relieved cryogenically pretreated specimens under dry and MQL conditions. The LPBF fabrication parameters were 200 W laser power, 600 mm/s scanning speed, 0.095 mm hatch spacing, and 60 𝜇 m layer thickness, while the cryogenic cycle consisted of cooling at 1 °C/min, soaking for 24 h, and reheating at 1 °C/min. Cryogenic treatment reduced the 𝛽 -phase fraction by approximately 48.5% relatively and lowered microhardness from 396.6 HV to 371.45 HV, which may be associated with increased ductility. Compared with untreated dry grinding, cryo-treated dry grinding reduced tangential force by about 21% and normal force by about 27.93%, while improving the F t /F n ratio. Surface roughness also decreased by roughly 17% under cryo-treated dry grinding. MQL further improved grinding performance by reducing friction and temperature at the grinding interface. The hybrid Cryogenic pretreatment with MQL condition produced the best overall results, yielding the lowest forces, the highest 𝐹 𝑡 ⁡ / 𝐹 𝑛 ratio, the smoothest surface finish, and the most favourable compressive residual stresses. Overall, the combined effect of cryogenic pretreatment and MQL demonstrated the greatest potential for improving grindability and surface integrity in AM Ti-64. ABSTRACT Single-point incremental forming (SPIF) offers substantial flexibility for manufacturing customized sheet-metal components without dedicated dies, but its wider application remains limited by the difficulty of relating forming-force evolution to fracture-controlled formability under different forming conditions. This study develops a numerical–experimental framework for the coupled assessment of forming forces and maximum forming height in the SPIF of AA1050 aluminum sheets. An explicit finite element model was established in ABAQUS using the Hill’48R anisotropic yield criterion and Kim–Tuan hardening model, together with an experimentally determined fracture forming limit (FFL) to identify fracture initiation. The model was evaluated against experiments for truncated-conical components with wall angles ranging from 65° to 90°. The predicted resultant forming forces show deviations of 3.34–6.20%, with an average deviation of approximately 4%, while the predicted maximum forming heights differ from the experimental values by only 0.41–0.94%. Increasing the wall angle intensifies thickness reduction and localized deformation, resulting in higher forming loads and a progressive reduction in fracture-controlled forming height from 14.67 mm at 65° to 9.18 mm at 90°. To complement conventional force–time curves, a spatial force-mapping procedure was developed by coupling the measured force histories with the instantaneous tool position and projecting the data onto standardized X–Y and X–Z coordinate grids. The resulting maps reveal the spatial distribution and evolution of forming loads, including force concentration along the toolpath and localized force changes associated with fracture-prone regions. The proposed framework therefore links forming-force response, tool position, forming depth, and fracture-controlled formability within a common analysis scheme. Within the AA1050, truncated-cone geometry, and process conditions investigated, the approach provides experimentally validated information for process analysis and parameter assessment. Its extension to other materials, geometries, and SPIF conditions, as well as real-time monitoring and data-driven process optimization, will require further calibration and experimental validation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+High-strain-rate+plastic+strengthening+of+wire+arc+additive+repaired+steel+layers+induced+&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.10.035%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 To improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of wire arc additive repairing (WAAR) layers, controlled explosive hardening (CEH) was proposed as a flexible non-rigid post-treatment method. An air gap and a polyurethane buffer layer were introduced to regulate shock-wave transmission, producing an effective plastic influence depth of approximately 3.5 mm. For ASTM A36 steel repaired with ER50-6 wire, theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, response-surface optimization, and confirmation experiments identified the preferred parameters as a charge thickness of 2.25 mm, an air gap of 4.12 mm, and a buffer-layer thickness of 2.13 mm. Under these conditions, shock energy was effectively transferred to the WAARed layer without obvious macroscopic damage. CEH did not alter the ferrite–pearlite phase constitution or cause pronounced overall grain refinement, but promoted dislocation accumulation, low-angle deformation substructures, local lattice rotation, and deformation twins. The representative continuous cementite-lamella segment length decreased from approximately 220 to 95 nm after CEH. The average hardness increased from 195.5 to 210.6 HV, while the yield strength increased by approximately 26% and the ultimate tensile strength reached 415–425 MPa. Residual tensile stress was also converted into a more uniform compressive state. The strengthening is attributed to the synergistic effects of dislocation and GND accumulation, low-angle deformation substructures, local twinning, and pearlite-lamella fragmentation. Abstract Pulsating forming techniques are advanced metal forming processes that apply cyclic or pulsed mechanical or hydraulic loads to the workpiece, enhancing formability and reducing defects compared to conventional static forming. Pulsating forming emerges as a transformative solution to overcome the intrinsic limitations of room-temperature formability in Ti–6Al–4V alloys. However, the lack of predictive, physics-based models hinders their industrial application. To address this gap in the literature, a novel hybrid finite element model was developed, which integrates a time-dependent Bergström dislocation model with the Gurson-Tvergaard-Needleman (GTN) damage criterion. The integration of stress relaxation, a pivotal mechanism in pulsating forming, was achieved through the modification of the Bergström model with a time-dependent differential equation. A correlation was established between this relaxation time and the GTN void nucleation parameter f N in order to directly simulate damage delay. The model was calibrated with monotonic tensile and relaxation tests, after which it was thoroughly validated against pulsating tensile and cylindrical cup hydroforming experiments. The accuracy of this method was subsequently demonstrated. The simulation showed an average error of 7.92 % for rupture pressures across nine cylindrical cup hydroforming scenarios. The present work provides a robust, physically based method that quantitatively links dislocation mechanisms, stress relaxation, and damage evolution, thereby establishing a foundation for model-driven design of advanced forming processes. Impact performance of lightweight lattice structures depends on both material properties and architectural topology, especially under localized versus global loading. This work examines the low-speed impact response of additively manufactured AlSi10Mg triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices through combined experimental and numerical methods. Nine sheet-based topologies at 25% relative density are tested under localized penetration (100–300 J), followed by crushing of four topologies across 15–25% relative density (20–60 J), with force-displacement response, deformation mechanics, and energy absorption systematically quantified. Diamond shows the highest penetration resistance (∼18.8 mm at 300 J), while Lidinoid shows the lowest, with full perforation already at 200 J. Finite element models incorporating calibrated Johnson-Cook plasticity and damage show good predictive capability for the Diamond and Gyroid topologies across all tested energies, and for all four topologies at 100 J, reproducing initial stiffness, crater formation, and force-penetration trends, with peak-force errors generally within 10%. Predictive accuracy decreases at higher energies and for the junction-dominated I-WP and Primitive topologies, where peak-force errors reach up to 44.7%, reflecting the framework's limits under unresolved manufacturing defects and discrete fracture. Topology exerts a first-order influence on impact response, supporting topology-specific selection of TPMS lattices for lightweight impact mitigation. item.title: The use of coupled nonlocal damage-plasticity to predict crack growth in ductile metal plates

fracture criterion on the computational predictability of wrought Inconel 718 [https://doi.org/10.1177/10567895261490276] 与《An incremental stress state dependent damage model for ductile failure prediction》共享 3 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.085 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1970499362, https://openalex.org/W2016463190, https://openalex.org/W2020242014 用户子程序与数值实现: 可作为显式积分算法、正则化方案与子程序实现细节的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移）
